newsitem.title: UK: LME copper crumbles, lead hits near 7-month low.
newsitem.headline: LME copper crumbles, lead hits near 7-month low.

text.p: Copper lost its nerve in the afternoon and ended near its lows after failing on the upside, pushing most of the other metals to fresh losses.
Trading was frenzied on the kerb as lead dived to its lowest for nearly seven months and alumimium dipped to a fresh nadir since June 1994.
"The Americans tried to get copper above $1,950 but when it failed everybody sold it off," one floor trader said, referring to U.S. speculative activity.
"The others were already weak, so that's all it took," he added.
Three months copper finished the kerb at $1,928, down $29 from Friday and just $2 off its low of the day.
Despite the bearish close. Tuesday's stocks data was expected to give prices some support.
The market expected a decline of 7,000-10,000 tonnes in inventories on Tuesday, after stocks shed 9,300 tonnes on Friday.
"We should have another good draw. Warrant sales are still strong," a floor trader said.
On Friday, prices spiked to a three-week high of $1,990 in the wake of the stocks decline and ahead of Wednesday's options declarations.
Spreads widened, with the cash/threes finishing at a $3/$5 contango.
Lead spiralled lower on the kerb, hitting $753, the lowest since March 7, and ended with a $22 loss at $756.
Stops were earlier triggered when prices slid through key support and were battered further when copper returned to its lows.
Aluminium also notched up fresh losses, edging below last Monday's low of $1,387.
Prices ended at $1,377.50, down $31.50 and only 50 cents off its low for the day. It was the weakest price since mid-June 1994, when the market hit $1,361.
Nickel followed the trend, crashing below last week's range and hitting a low of $7,060. Prices, however, recovered to $7,100 by the end of the kerb, ending with a $110 loss.
Zinc shed $8 to $1,016 and tin fell $50 to $6,020.
